guide: Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: target margin, hour cost, safety cash, tax set-aside share, months of cash cover, draw limit and overhead share per project.
Fill Projects once; every other sheet looks up the project name, the client and the type from it. Keep the project ids the same in all your workbooks.

Each month fill Profit and Loss: fee income, FF&E sales, trades re-billed, product and trades cost, labour at hour cost and overheads. Revenue, margin before labour, net result and margin share fill in.
Open Project Results to see the margin after labour, the margin per hour and whether each project reached the target margin and covered its overhead share.

Record the cash on Cash Flow by Month, then keep 13-week Cash Forecast current every week: expected receipts, vendor and trade payments, payroll, owner draw, overheads and tax. A red row means cash falls below your safety level.
Log every cost on Expenses and set a monthly budget for each category on Overhead Budget. Payroll, Owner Draw and Business Tax hold the people, owner and tax payments.
Use Marketing Results and Source Value to see which source brings projects that pay, and Client Value and Reviews to see which clients are worth keeping.
Write your goals on Goals, review prices on Pricing Review and track renewals on Insurance and Renewals. Receivables Ageing and Payables Ageing show who owes you and whom you owe.

Use the 14 calculators for project margin, break-even, price changes, the cash forecast, owner draw, tax instalments, marketing cost, client value, fee mix, hiring, overhead budget, growth, safety cash and a what-if grid.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Finance Dashboard and Charts at every month-end and at the weekly money review.

listing.title: Interior Designer Finance Excel Template: Profit and Loss, Project Margin, 13-week Cash Forecast, Owner Draw, Tax, Break-even
listing.headline: Know what your studio really earns and what is coming
listing.description:
Run the money side of an interior design studio in one Excel workbook. Profit and Loss shows fee income, FF&E (furniture, fittings and equipment) sales and trades re-billed against product cost, trades cost, labour and overheads, month by month, with the margin before labour, the net result and the margin share worked out for you. Project Results shows what every project earned after labour, per project and per hour, and whether it reached your target margin and covered its share of the overheads.

Cash Flow by Month and the 13-week Cash Forecast show what came in and went out and what is coming: expected receipts from open invoices against vendor and trade payments, payroll, owner draw, overheads and business tax, with a red flag when cash falls below your safety level. Expenses, Overhead Budget, Payroll, Owner Draw and Business Tax keep every payment, and Receivables Ageing and Payables Ageing show who owes you and whom you owe by age.

Marketing Results and Source Value show which source brings the projects that pay, Client Value ranks clients by margin and payment habits, Reviews keeps your ratings, Goals tracks your targets, Pricing Review shows what a price change does to your margin and Insurance and Renewals keeps your dates. 14 calculators cover project margin and break-even hours, studio break-even in projects, price review impact, a cash forecast planner, a safe owner draw, a tax instalment planner, marketing cost per project, client lifetime value, fee mix, a hiring check, an overhead budget check, growth, safety cash and a projects and margin what-if grid. Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and send 28 ready text messages that open with the details already written in.

This is part eight of the Interior Designer suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data for a small design studio to explore first. It helps you plan your finances and does not promise results or give tax advice.

paragraphs: Annual business review of {set:company}, page for the month starting {col:pl.month}, prepared on {today}.
Revenue of the month: {col:pl.revenue}. Margin before labour: {col:pl.margin_before}. Net result: {col:pl.net_result}, a margin share of {col:pl.margin_share}.
Cost of labour at hour cost: {col:pl.labour}. Overheads: {col:pl.overheads}.
Before the review meeting, also read the goals, the pricing review, the client value and source value sheets and write down three changes for next year.
Sign the page when the owner and the accountant have both read it.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.

documents.title: Pricing proposal for a rate or fee change
paragraphs: Pricing proposal of {set:company}, dated {today}. Item {col:pricing.price_id}: {col:pricing.item}.
Current price: {col:pricing.current_price} {col:pricing.unit}. Proposed price: {col:pricing.proposed}. Change: {col:pricing.change_pct}. Direction: {col:pricing.direction}.
Expected effect on the yearly margin: {col:pricing.effect_margin}. Status: {col:pricing.status}. Decision date: {col:pricing.decision_date}.
Tell current clients in good time and apply the new price only to new proposals and new agreements.

documents.title: Review summary for the owner
paragraphs: Review summary of {set:company}, dated {today}. Review {col:reviews.review_id} of {col:reviews.date}, received by {col:reviews.source}.
Client: {col:reviews.client}. Project: {col:reviews.project} ({col:reviews.project_id}). Rating: {col:reviews.rating} out of {col:reviews.top}, {col:reviews.band}.
Comment: {col:reviews.comment}. Would recommend the studio: {col:reviews.recommend}.
Reply within two days, thank the client and share any useful point with the team.

documents.title: Goals and targets report
paragraphs: Goals and targets report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Goal {col:goals.goal_id}: {col:goals.goal} ({col:goals.kind}). Owner: {col:goals.owner}.
Target: {col:goals.target} {col:goals.unit}. Actual: {col:goals.actual}. Progress: {col:goals.progress}. Due date: {col:goals.due_date}.
Time used so far: {col:goals.time_share}. Check: {col:goals.state}.
If a goal is behind, write one action, one owner and one date on the sheet and review it at the next weekly money review.
